text.p: Negotiations between the United States and the two Koreas, due to resume on Friday, have been delayed and North Korean officials said they had to consult with their government in Pyongyang.

The negotiations, to secure North Korea's agreement to join in four-party peace talks that would also include China, had been set to resume at 10 a.m. (1400 GMT) but had not started more than one hour after that time.
The three delegations held an inconclusive meeting on Wednesday in New York but all sides reported progress and said they hoped to settle the issue when they resumed.

A spokesman for North Korea's mission to the United Nations, who declined to be identified, told Reuters after his country's team failed to arrive for the Friday morning session on time: "We need to contact with capitals." Asked if there was a problem, he said: "I cannot say anything in connection with that."
U.S. officials said only that they had been told by the North Koreans that they would be late.

The meeting was called to hear Pyongyang's formal response to a year-old U.S.-South Korean proposal for peace talks that would finally close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing the fraying armistice with a peace treaty.
